questions.q: In a company income statement, which term normally describes sales before deducting expenses?
options: Revenue
Net profit
Retained earnings
Operating margin
questions.explanation: Revenue désigne les ventes ou revenus selon le contexte. Le bénéfice et la marge sont des résultats obtenus après prise en compte de certaines charges.

questions.q: Profit is defined as revenue minus total expenses. Both revenue and expenses rose, but profit fell. Which relationship must hold?
options: Revenue and expenses necessarily increased by the same percentage.
The absolute increase in expenses exceeded the absolute increase in revenue.
Revenue and expenses increased by the same absolute amount.
The absolute increase in expenses was less than the absolute increase in revenue.
questions.explanation: La variation du résultat est la hausse absolue des revenus moins la hausse absolue des charges. Pour que le résultat baisse, la seconde doit dépasser la première ; comparer seulement les taux ne suffit pas.

questions.q: A translator renders “annual revenue” as “bénéfice annuel” in a sales report. What is the main problem?
options: Assets are being confused with liabilities.
A forecast is being confused with an audit opinion.
Sales are being confused with profit.
Annual figures are being confused with monthly figures.
questions.explanation: La traduction change l’indicateur : revenue renvoie ici aux ventes, tandis que bénéfice suppose la prise en compte des charges. La période annuelle est conservée.

questions.q: A human resources report states: “Staff turnover fell following the retention programme.” What does turnover refer to here?
options: Sales made during the financial year
Inventories sold during the month
Profit retained within the company
Employees leaving and being replaced
questions.explanation: Le contexte des ressources humaines et de la fidélisation désigne la rotation du personnel. Turnover ne signifie chiffre d’affaires que dans certains contextes commerciaux.

questions.q: A supplier asks about a business’s “annual turnover” to assess its sales volume. Which reply answers the question?
options: Our annual sales were €800,000.
Our annual net profit was €80,000.
Our closing bank balance was €40,000.
Our total assets were €600,000.
questions.explanation: Dans ce contexte commercial, annual turnover désigne le chiffre d’affaires annuel. Le bénéfice, la trésorerie et les actifs mesurent des réalités différentes.

questions.q: A summary replaces “operating profit” with “net profit” without any further information. Why is this unsafe?
options: The two terms necessarily relate to different years.
The two terms can exclude different categories of expenses.
Net profit always means the amount of cash collected.
Operating profit is another term for annual revenue.
questions.explanation: Le résultat opérationnel et le résultat net n’intègrent pas nécessairement les mêmes produits et charges. Il faut préserver le niveau de résultat annoncé par la source.

questions.q: Which English term normally refers to costs recognised in an income statement?
options: Equity
Borrowings
Expenses
Receipts
questions.explanation: Expenses correspond ici aux charges du compte de résultat. Les receipts sont des encaissements, les borrowings des emprunts et equity les capitaux propres.

questions.q: An accountant records an unpaid December electricity bill as a December expense. Which statement preserves the distinction between accounting and cash?
options: The payment has already reduced the bank balance.
No expense can exist until the supplier is paid.
The unpaid bill is automatically a sales receipt.
The expense is recognised before the bill is paid.
questions.explanation: La reconnaissance d’une charge et son paiement peuvent intervenir à des dates différentes. Une facture non réglée ne prouve donc pas un décaissement en décembre.

questions.q: A cash budget labels every outgoing payment “expense”, including repayment of loan principal. Which approach correctly distinguishes cash from accounting?
options: Separate cash payments from expenses; loan principal repayment reduces a debt.
Treat the whole principal repayment as interest expense for the period.
Classify every outgoing payment as an operating expense regardless of its purpose.
Recognise an expense only when an invoice is paid, regardless of when it was incurred.
questions.explanation: Un décaissement n’est pas nécessairement une charge : le principal remboursé réduit une dette. Il faut aussi distinguer la date de paiement d’une facture de la reconnaissance de la charge.

questions.q: A manager says: “We cut travel expenses, although sales were unchanged.” Which interpretation is supported?
options: The company’s liabilities necessarily disappeared.
One category of costs decreased.
Every category of costs decreased.
Sales receipts necessarily increased.
questions.explanation: La phrase établit une baisse des frais de déplacement uniquement. Elle ne décrit ni toutes les charges, ni les encaissements, ni l’ensemble des dettes.

questions.q: A note says “expenses were incurred in March and paid in April”. Which French summary is accurate?
options: Les ventes concernent mars et leur règlement intervient en avril.
Les dépenses ont été annulées avant tout paiement.
Les charges concernent mars et le paiement intervient en avril.
Les charges et le paiement concernent uniquement avril.
questions.explanation: Incurred décrit ici le rattachement de la charge, tandis que paid désigne le règlement. Les confondre effacerait le décalage entre résultat et trésorerie.

questions.q: Which balance-sheet term refers to resources recognised as belonging to or controlled by a business?
options: Liabilities
Expenses
Revenue
Assets
questions.explanation: Assets désigne les actifs reconnus au bilan. Les liabilities correspondent aux dettes et autres passifs hors capitaux propres ; charges et revenus relèvent du résultat.

questions.q: A customer owes the company money for goods already delivered. How should “trade receivable” be understood?
options: An amount due from a customer
An amount due to a supplier
An amount invested by a shareholder
An amount distributed as a dividend
questions.explanation: Une créance client est une somme à recevoir du client. Elle ne doit pas être inversée avec une dette fournisseur, somme que l’entreprise doit à un tiers.

questions.q: A report lists a bank loan under “liabilities”. What does this classification communicate?
options: The company has already repaid the whole loan.
The company owes an obligation to a lender.
The lender owns all the company’s equipment.
The loan is part of the company’s sales revenue.
questions.explanation: Le classement en liabilities indique une obligation envers un prêteur. Il ne transforme pas l’emprunt en ventes et ne démontre pas que la dette est déjà remboursée.

questions.q: A translation uses “equity” and “liabilities” interchangeably in a balance-sheet analysis. What distinction has been lost?
options: Gross profit versus operating profit
Cash receipts versus cash payments
Shareholders’ interest versus obligations owed to others
Current sales versus sales in a previous year
questions.explanation: Equity correspond aux capitaux propres ; liabilities désigne les dettes et autres passifs reconnus hors capitaux propres. Leur confusion déforme la structure du financement.

questions.q: A business buys equipment that will serve for several years. In a balance-sheet description, which heading is relevant to that equipment?
options: Revenue
Trade payables only
Share capital only
Assets
questions.explanation: Le matériel reconnu au bilan constitue un actif. La façon dont il est financé peut créer une dette, mais cette dette ne remplace pas le classement du matériel lui-même.

questions.q: An English summary translates “trade payables” as “créances clients”. What is the correct interpretation?
options: Amounts owed to suppliers
Amounts owed by customers
Amounts paid by shareholders
Amounts kept as cash reserves
questions.explanation: Trade payables désigne les dettes fournisseurs. Les créances clients se traduisent par trade receivables : le sens du flux à payer ou à recevoir est essentiel.

questions.q: What does “cash flow” primarily describe?
options: The number of products held in inventory
Movements of cash into and out of a business
Profit after every accounting adjustment
The total market value of a business
questions.explanation: Cash flow renvoie aux flux de trésorerie. Il ne constitue pas un synonyme automatique du bénéfice, de la valeur de marché ou des quantités stockées.

questions.q: A company reports a profit but many customers have not paid their invoices. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: Unpaid invoices must have no effect on cash collection.
A profitable company cannot have a cash shortage.
Profit does not by itself prove that cash is available.
Profit proves that every customer has paid.
questions.explanation: Le résultat peut intégrer des ventes encore non encaissées. Un bénéfice positif ne suffit donc pas à démontrer que l’entreprise dispose de liquidités immédiatement.

questions.q: A company receives a new bank loan. Which description of the immediate cash movement is accurate?
options: It is sales revenue from customers.
It is profit from selling inventory.
It is a cash outflow to suppliers.
It is a cash inflow from financing.
questions.explanation: L’encaissement d’un emprunt apporte de la trésorerie au titre du financement. Il ne constitue ni un chiffre d’affaires commercial ni un bénéfice issu des ventes.

questions.q: A note reports revenue and expenses, not cash movements. Which information addresses the gap between those accounting figures and the related operating receipts and payments?
options: The timing of related cash settlements and any non-cash items.
Changes in share capital and the total dividends declared.
Equipment purchase payments and repayments of loan principal.
The movement in the company’s share price and market value.
questions.explanation: Les décalages de règlement et les éléments non monétaires distinguent le résultat des flux liés aux opérations concernées. Financement, investissement et valeur de marché relèvent d’autres périmètres.

questions.q: A company sells an old machine and receives payment immediately. Which wording reports the cash fact without assuming a profit?
options: The sale was an operating expense paid in cash.
The sale generated a cash inflow.
The sale necessarily generated an accounting profit.
The sale increased trade payables.
questions.explanation: Le règlement reçu est bien une entrée de trésorerie. Pour conclure à un profit de cession, il faudrait aussi connaître la valeur comptable et les coûts éventuels.
